description: Fixture cases for the Case File export (case_file.py). Each case is seeded into a temporary SQLite DB through the real storage path (case_store.create_case / save_message / assistant_content_for_storage), with sources built by grounded_answer.sources_from_ids() from real parsed-corpus chunks. 'verified' lists the chunk ids the claim verifier reported as supporting a supported/partially-supported claim; 'unverified' lists cited chunks whose claims did not pass; 'verification': 'not_recorded' simulates an answer saved before verification was persisted.

cases.description: Consumer case with a confirmed receipt document (facts from it must name the document), a dated purchase, and one unverified source that must be excluded.
cases.title: Defective Product Refund

conversation_state.case_summary: The user bought a phone from Croma that stopped working within a week; the seller refuses a refund.

turns.user: I bought a phone and it stopped working after 5 days. The seller is refusing to refund me. What can I do?

reply.issue_summary: This looks like a consumer complaint about defective goods and a refused refund.
evidence_to_preserve: Messages or emails with the seller

turns.user: I sent the seller a written complaint on 20 March 2026 & they still haven't replied.

reply.message: Got it — I've added that to the current case.

cases.description: Cyber case where the user corrects a count: 'actually it was 3 transactions, not 2'. The old fact must be replaced, not shown alongside.

cases.description: Tenancy case with no full dates anywhere ('last week' only): Timeline must be omitted; no evidence items or documents, so Evidence is omitted too. Two chunks of the same provision must de-duplicate to one law entry.

turns.user: Mere landlord ne last week bijli kaat di kyunki maine rent late diya. Main Delhi mein rehta hoon.

cases.description: Sources include case law, a compiled summary and official guidance -- each must carry its own label. A second answer has no verification record (saved before it was persisted) and its source must be left out with a note.
cases.title: Misleading Green Advertisement

conversation_state.case_summary: A brand advertised a product as '100% eco-friendly'; the user paid more for it and found the claim was false.

turns.user: A brand advertised its bottle as 100% eco-friendly and I paid extra for it on 2026-07-14, but it turned out to be ordinary plastic.

reply.issue_summary: This may be a misleading environmental claim (greenwashing) in an advertisement.
evidence_to_preserve: Screenshot or copy of the advertisement

turns.user: Do I have to pay a fee to complain?

reply.issue_summary: Fees for consumer complaints depend on the value of the claim.

facts_exclude: Do I have to pay a fee

law_labels.Greenwashing: Compiled summary — not the official text of the law
